title: Power & Mass Training by Gene Mozee
author: Mithosphere
desc:
The core purpose of this 3-day full-body routine is to simultaneously force the development of absolute physical power and dense, quality muscle mass by targeting the body’s deep-lying auxiliary muscle fibers.

Based on the training philosophy of old-school icons John Farbotnik and Marvin Eder, this program is designed to break through training plateaus. It eliminates the filler, high-volume isolation work that often leads to overtraining, replacing it with a concentrated attack on the major muscle groups. The specific physiological and practical goals of the routine include:

 Activating Deep Muscle Fibers: According to the "all-or-none" law of muscle contraction, light weights only recruit superficial muscle fibers. This program relies on heavy compound lifts to deliberately force the deep-lying, auxiliary fibers to thicken, resulting in greater muscular girth, density, and fullness.

Systemic Growth via Compound Movement: By focusing entirely on heavy weapons like squats, bench presses, rows, and overhead presses, the program triggers a massive systemic growth response. Forcing progression on these core exercises causes related primary, secondary, and tertiary muscle groups to automatically grow alongside them.

Periodized Strength Waves: Rather than keeping the body at a stagnant weight or rep scheme, the program waves volume and intensity across 3.5 months. It builds a base at 8 reps, increases sets to 6-8 reps, forces heavy neurological adaptation with a 5x5-7 framework, and peaks with absolute strength work at 3-5 reps. This forced adaptation ensures that as the muscles get stronger, they are continually challenged with heavier poundages to maximize fiber recruitment.

Optimizing Recovery and Efficiency: Training on 3 alternate days a week ensures that the central nervous system and muscle tissues have ample time to rest, recover, and grow. It proves that maximum muscle mass does not require living in the gym; it requires brief, high-intensity efforts paired with radical recovery, high-protein nutrition, and sound sleep.

Ultimately, the routine operates under a simple, scientific formula: handling consistently heavier poundages over time equals maximum mass and power.

ex.note: Keep the feet fairly close together. Squat to slightly below parallel, keeping your knees pointing forward. Exhale strongly at the hard spot on the way up.
Use a medium-wide grip, with your hands about 26 to 32 inches apart. Lower the bar slowly to the highest point on your chest and immediately ram it back to the top as you exhale.
Use the same as for the bench press. Pull the bar up until it touches the rib cage. Lower the bar slowly close to your body, but don’t let it touch the floor. Use some cheat on the last few reps.
Use a slightly wider-than-shoulder-width grip. Keep your entire body tight and exhale as you press the weight up. Do the reps rapidly without pausing at the top or bottom.
Using a fairly wide grip with your hands six to eight inches wider than shoulder-width, pull the bar down to just below your collar bones until it touches your upper chest.
Use a slight cheating motion as you inhale, curling the bells upward until they touch your delts. Exhale as you lower them all the way to straight arms.
